correctness.rationale: Let p_i denote three oriented branch-to-branch path sums of lengths a<=b<=c. A chain extension on cycles forces q_i=z+x,z+y,z in rank-two homology. For fixed cointegral basis B, distributing each q_i equally along the path is optimal and turns ||s|| into inf_z max(||z+x||/a,||z+y||/b,||z||/c). The dimension-two isometry (u,v)->(u+v,u-v) maps l1 balls to l_infty boxes, where triple intersection is equivalent to pairwise intersection, giving max(||x-y||/(a+b),||x||/(a+c),||y||/(b+c)). Cointegral bases correspond to independent integral coordinate columns u,v. All ||u||1,||v||1,||u-v||1>=1, at least one >=2, and unimodular witnesses put 2 on the largest denominator b+c. Therefore exactly max(1/(a+b),2/(b+c)); rational witness/centers suffice for every subfield F⊂R. Independently tested 120 sorted length triples through length 8 and rational optimization. The infinite statement follows from the integer lower bound, not finite cases.
